studies.title: Hubbard Glacier
studies.story: NASA’s radar comparison shows debris deposited by earthquake-triggered avalanches and landslides across the St. Elias Mountains. This replaces the October 2026 pair as the active Hubbard story.
limitations: NASA-published false-color visualizations derived from NISAR GSLC; these are not our own HH/HV exports or a numerical difference layer.
The prior October 2026 identification QA failures remain unresolved. This replacement pair has not received an independent product-level QA review.
studies.nextStep: Identify the event-spanning source granules and complete independent compatibility and QA checks before numerical analysis.

studies.title: Sossusvlei
studies.event: Two scene previews; no event established
studies.story: Official frequency-A HH and HV scene previews reveal the Namib’s dune and terrain patterns. All four local files match NASA’s catalog file sizes and MD5 checksums.
limitations: Browse-image integrity does not establish temporal change, geospatial alignment or a fixed common display scale.
Official identification QA failures remain unresolved. The prior 85,095-pixel screening counts have not been revalidated; numerical ROI and difference exports are pending.
studies.nextStep: Recover the screened ROI checkpoint and numerical source arrays before producing any quantitative comparison.

studies.title: Krasheninnikov
studies.story: NASA’s 17-frame NISAR sequence follows a lava field expanding from the northern crater. It is a documented example of landscape change during an ongoing eruption.
limitations: The sequence begins after eruption onset, so its first frame is not a pre-eruption baseline.
This is NASA’s published visualization. We have not selected or numerically processed the underlying granules.
studies.nextStep: Recover the sequence’s granule list and select compatible acquisitions for a bounded lava-field review.

studies.title: Limpopo & Incomati
studies.story: NASA’s NISAR GCOV visualizations show the river basins before and during extensive flooding. The published composites use a consistent color scale across the two dates.
limitations: False-color publisher visualizations combine HH, HV and their ratio. They are not individual HH/HV science rasters.
We have not reproduced NASA’s flood classifications or calculated flooded area.
studies.nextStep: Locate the two GCOV acquisitions and validate a bounded ROI before generating our own backscatter statistics.

A compatible NISAR-only before/after pair and its individual acquisition dates have not been verified here.

studies.title: The Antarctic “hummingbird”
studies.story: NASA’s L-band scene shows ice fractured as it flows around a protruding mountaintop. The striking colors describe radar scattering and ice structure.
limitations: This is a documented NISAR scene, not a before/after record of a calving event.
An exact acquisition day and a compatible temporal pair have not been verified here.
studies.nextStep: Identify the source acquisition and a later compatible observation before evaluating temporal change.

studies.title: Etna
studies.story: NASA CMR confirms a matching NISAR GCOV pair spanning Etna’s August 6 eruptive episode. Both scenes cover the summit at 15°E, 37.75°N, use descending track 51 / frame 69, and share frequency-A HH/HV and product version 1.0.11. The four browse images match the catalog sizes and MD5 hashes.
limitations: Pair spans the August episode, not the December 2025/January 2026 eruption originally proposed.
A permanent instrument gap from July 27 to August 10 leaves a 24-day interval across the episode; intermediate evolution is unobserved.
Both official QA summaries returned HTTP 401; Earthdata credentials are not configured here. QA contents and scientific calibration have not been independently verified.
Browse colors are not numerical radar power; no lava mapping, displacement, or difference image has been generated.
studies.nextStep: Authenticate with Earthdata to retrieve official QA, then inspect numerical HDF5 grids, common valid pixels and calibration before producing a fixed-scale ROI comparison.

studies.title: Cyclone Senyar
studies.story: NASA documents widespread flooding in northern Sumatra using Landsat 9. The event is a promising target for checking whether NISAR captured the flood extent through clouds.
limitations: A direct NASA CMR search across northern Sumatra (95–100.5°E, 0–6°N) returned no NISAR L0–L3 products for November 1–December 31, 2025. This does not prove the satellite never acquired data.
The Lhoksukon GCOV search first returned observations on June 21, 2026; those dates cannot show the November 2025 flood.
NASA’s event imagery is Landsat 9. No comparable NISAR event pair or flood measurement has been verified.
studies.nextStep: Recheck for released or reprocessed event-period NISAR coverage; retain the documented Landsat event context until a compatible NISAR pair becomes available.

studies.title: Cyclone Koji
studies.story: Australia’s Bureau of Meteorology documents Cyclone Koji and extensive rainfall and flooding. It is a candidate for an Australian NISAR flood study.
limitations: The December 29, 2025 / January 10, 2026 track-23 GCOV pair is real, but both dates precede Koji’s January 11 landfall. It cannot be used as a before/after Koji comparison.
No processed post-landfall scene was found for the central/eastern Queensland target through February 10. A wider state search through February 28 found only raw L0B records outside that target.
No verified event-spanning NISAR pair, flood-area statistic or displacement result is available here.
studies.nextStep: Recheck the processed NISAR archive for post-landfall coverage of the affected target; the available pre-landfall and June-onward scenes do not fill this gap.
